# lean-pkg palomar

Palomar: prepare (build a submission bundle), check (read-only readiness), port-modules (plan or write the module-system port); no network.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg palomar [common flags] [COMMAND]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Subcommands

- [`lean-pkg palomar prepare`](#lean-pkg-palomar-prepare): build the submission bundle (formalization.yaml, comparator configs, receipts, README.txt, MANIFEST.sha256); event palomar-prepared
- [`lean-pkg palomar check`](#lean-pkg-palomar-check): read-only, offline: every gap to Palomar's mechanical rules at one commit (module headers, toolchain floor, comparator configs, formalization.yaml, licence, repository); exit 0 ready / 1 gaps
- [`lean-pkg palomar port-modules`](#lean-pkg-palomar-port-modules): plan (dry run, default) or --write the mechanical port of the package's tracked .lean files to Lean's module system; never commits

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## lean-pkg palomar prepare

build the submission bundle (formalization.yaml, comparator configs, receipts, README.txt, MANIFEST.sha256); event palomar-prepared.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg palomar prepare [--out DIR] [--dry-run] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--out DIR` | bundle directory (default &lt;checkout&gt;/.lean-receipts/palomar-&lt;HEAD12&gt;/); must not exist or be empty |
| `--dry-run` | run every check and print the plan; write nothing |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `palomar prepare NAME` | build a Palomar submission bundle; no network request, nothing submitted. Default directory `<checkout>/.lean-receipts/palomar-<HEAD12>/` (`--out DIR` elsewhere; an existing non-empty target is refused, never overwritten): `formalization.yaml` (the renderer's output, schema-valid; placeholders are warnings), `configs/<path>` (every comparator configuration tracked at HEAD, byte-identical, and the [headline configuration](../comparator.md#headline-configuration-the-papers-main-results) when one is declared; README.txt names it for the main-results entry and its `record` command; JSON `headline_config`), `receipts/<file>` (the recorded gate and comparator receipts, validated against HEAD: bound to it or to an evidence-only ancestor), `README.txt` (the manual steps, the Palomar URLs and the `record ... palomar-submitted` command), `MANIFEST.sha256` (`sha256  path` per file; `sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256`). Refused (exit 1, nothing written, `--dry-run` included) without either receipt or when one is not bound to HEAD, without consent, when the render fails the schema, when `palomar check` finds any `error` gap at HEAD (each listed as `✗  CODE: detail` with its fix; `warn` gaps never refuse and print as `lean-pkg: warning: palomar check: ...`), or on blocking `public-safety` hits in the bundle (scanned like a fresh-history export). Records `palomar-prepared` {commit, bundle, bundle_sha256 (sha256 of MANIFEST.sha256)}. `--dry-run` runs every check and prints the plan, writing nothing. `--json`: {ok, name, dry_run, bundle, commit, configs[], files[], bundle_sha256, placeholders[], public_safety {block_hits, warn_hits}, palomar_check {ready, commit, errors, warns, codes[], command}, manuscript_findings, warnings[], event}; `manuscript_findings` is the claims ledger's summary of what the formalization found in the manuscript (one text line when there is one; not in the bundle, never a refusal) | `[--out DIR]` `[--dry-run]` |

## lean-pkg palomar check

read-only, offline: every gap to Palomar's mechanical rules at one commit (module headers, toolchain floor, comparator configs, formalization.yaml, licence, repository); exit 0 ready / 1 gaps.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg palomar check [--rev REV] [--config PATH] [--rules FILE] [--repo DIR]
                       [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--rev REV` | the commit to judge (default: the gate-bound commit, else HEAD) |
| `--config PATH` | judge only this comparator configuration (Palomar verifies the one a submission names); default: every configuration tracked at the commit |
| `--rules FILE` | a newer PalomarSubmission browser-preflight-policy.json (schema 1) downloaded by hand; default: the rules pinned at PalomarSubmission d4e41c1d5b0d (read 2026-10-16) |
| `--repo DIR` | judge the checkout DIR instead of the registered local_path (never saved) |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `palomar check NAME` | read-only and offline (no network, nothing written, no event): every gap between the package at one commit (`--rev REV`, else the gate-bound commit, else HEAD; git objects, never the working tree) and Palomar's mechanical rules, pinned at PalomarSubmission `d4e41c1d5b0d` (read 2026-10-16; `--rules FILE` takes a newer `browser-preflight-policy.json`): a `module` header in every tracked `.lean` file of the repository (exact list of the files without one), at most 10,000 lines, no symlinks; the toolchain floor v4.35.0-rc2; a Lake configuration, no submodules; each comparator configuration (`--config PATH`: only that one) with the required keys, no other keys (`judged_as`, `lean_pkg_scaffold` are refused), standard axioms, tracked module sources, a Challenge within 1,000 lines and 100 KiB; the headline configuration, when declared: the same checks, plus `comparator.headline_uncovered` (error) or `comparator.headline_unjudged` (warn) from the subset rule (JSON `headline` {config, source, judged, covered} or null); `formalization.yaml` tracked, v0.4-valid, no placeholders, Palomar's metadata minimum; one root licence file matching `license_spdx`; a GitHub repository, public, the commit pushed (these two `warn`). Each gap `{code, severity error\|warn, paths, detail, fix}`; verdict first and last; `--repo DIR` judges another checkout; exit 0 no `error` gap, 1 error gaps, 2 usage ([rules, source and date](../faq.md#palomar-readiness)) | `[--rev REV]` `[--config PATH]` `[--rules FILE]` `[--repo DIR]` |

### JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `palomar-check` (exit 1): `commit`, `commit_source`, `configs`, `counts`, `gaps`, `headline`, `lean_files`, `lean_toolchain`, `missing_module`, `name`, `not_checked`, `ok`, `project_path`, `ready`, `repo_override`, `rules`

## lean-pkg palomar port-modules

plan (dry run, default) or --write the mechanical port of the package's tracked .lean files to Lean's module system; never commits.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg palomar port-modules [--dry-run] [--write] [--agent AGENT] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--dry-run` | the default: print the per-file plan and the unified diff; write nothing |
| `--write` | apply the plan to a clean working tree (a dirty tree is refused); never commits, never writes the registry |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --write: the lease holder, when the package is leased |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `palomar port-modules NAME` | the mechanical port of the package's tracked `.lean` files to Lean's module system, which Palomar requires (`palomar check`: `source.module_required`). Reads git objects at HEAD; a dry run by default (`--dry-run`): a per-file report and a unified diff, nothing written. Per file without a `module` header: `module` inserted as the first command (after leading blanks and ordinary comments; before a `/-! -/` or `/-- -/`, which are commands), each header `import X` rewritten to `public import X` (`meta import X` to `public meta import X`; `import all`, `private` and `public` forms kept, never `public import all`), the body after the imports (and after the module docstrings that follow them) wrapped in `public section` ... `end` (no `end` when a `namespace`/`section` is still open at the end of the file). A module-headed file is skipped, so a second run is a no-op. Refused per file, with the reason: a `prelude` file (port it by hand), a file that is not UTF-8, a symlink. Reported for review, never auto-fixed (`review [CODE]`, lines of the ported file): `expose` (a `def` that another file unfolds with `unfold`, `delta`, `simp [d]`, `rw [d]`, `d.eq_def`, or reduces on a line with `rfl`/`decide`: add `@[expose]`; `abbrev` and instances are already exposed), `private` (a private name in a public statement is an unknown identifier), `meta` (`#eval`, `native_decide`, `initialize`: code from another module needs a `meta import`), `imports-non-module` (a module cannot import a non-module file or dependency), `scope-balance`. Only the package's files: `.lake/`, `lake-packages/`, nested Lake projects and `path` dependencies are excluded and `lakefile.lean` is exempt. `--write` applies the plan to a clean working tree (a modified or untracked path, a refused file, or a foreign live lease without `--agent HOLDER` refuses, exit 1, nothing written); it never commits and never writes the registry, and prints the follow-ups: `lake build`, the `@[expose]` review, `lean-pkg palomar check NAME` after the commit, and for a gated package a new gate (the sources changed). Exit 0, or 1 when a file is refused. `--json`: {ok, name, dry_run, written[], commit, project_path, files[{path, action port\|skip\|refused, reason, edits[], reviews[{code, line, detail}]}], counts{port, skip, refused, review}, expose[], excluded[], vendored_dirs[], outside_package, diff, follow_ups[]} | `[--dry-run \| --write]` `[--agent A]` |

### JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `palomar-port-modules` (exit 0): `commit`, `counts`, `diff`, `dry_run`, `excluded`, `expose`, `files`, `follow_ups`, `name`, `ok`, `outside_package`, `project_path`, `vendored_dirs`, `written`
